title: PAROXYSMAL EXTREME PAIN DISORDER
alt_titles: PAIN, SUBMANDIBULAR, OCULAR, AND RECTAL, WITH FLUSHING

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that paroxysmal extreme pain disorder (PEXPD) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SCN9A gene, which encodes the sodium channel Nav1.7.

checks.claim: Paroxysmal extreme pain disorder (PEXPD) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SCN9A gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Paroxysmal extreme pain disorder (PEPD) is a rare autosomal dominant pain disorder linked to a mutation in the SCN9A gene
checks.explanation: Autosomal dominant inheritance linked to SCN9A mutation means the disorder is caused by heterozygous mutation; the case also has a heterozygous mutation.

checks.claim: The SCN9A gene encodes the sodium channel Nav1.7.
checks.evidence_quote: the candidate gene SCN9A, which encodes hNa(v)1.7
checks.explanation: The abstract states that SCN9A encodes Nav1.7.

paragraphs.text: Paroxysmal extreme pain disorder (PEXPD), previously known as familial rectal pain, is an inherited condition marked by attacks of rectal, ocular, or submandibular pain with flushing (Fertleman et al., 2006). Onset is in the neonatal period or infancy and the disorder lasts throughout life. Autonomic signs are most prominent early on. These include skin flushing, harlequin color change, tonic attacks, and syncope with bradycardia. Later, attacks of excruciating deep burning pain predominate. Defecation, cold wind, eating, and emotion can trigger these attacks (Fertleman et al., 2007).

paragraphs.text: Through an international consortium, Fertleman et al. (2007) collected clinical data on 77 affected individuals from 15 families. Fourteen affected individuals completed a validated pain questionnaire. Onset was in the neonatal period or infancy, and the disorder persisted throughout life. Autonomic manifestations predominated at first. All patients had skin flushing, and most had harlequin color change and tonic attacks. Dramatic syncopes with bradycardia, and sometimes asystole, were common. Later, patients had attacks of excruciating deep burning pain, often in the rectal, ocular, or jaw areas but sometimes diffuse. Triggers included defecation, cold wind, eating, and emotion.

paragraphs.text: Fertleman et al. (2006) performed a genome-wide linkage search followed by mutation analysis of the candidate gene SCN9A. They identified 8 missense mutations in 11 families with PEXPD and in 2 sporadic cases. In vitro functional analysis of 3 of the mutant Nav1.7 channels showed reduced fast inactivation, which led to persistent sodium current.

paragraphs.text: Fertleman et al. (2006) noted that other SCN9A mutations, which shift the activation threshold to more negative values, cause primary erythermalgia. Carbamazepine is effective in PEXPD but not in primary erythermalgia. In their study, carbamazepine selectively blocked the persistent current of PEXPD mutant channels but did not affect the negative activation threshold of a primary erythermalgia mutant. The authors concluded that PEXPD and primary erythermalgia are allelic disorders with distinct biophysical mechanisms.

checks.explanation: The abstract states that other SCN9A mutations with more negative activation thresholds cause primary erythermalgia.
